label: Gene Huff
narrative: Gene Huff has two distinct roles in this cluster and the board should carry both, because the second is the structural one. He is a Las Vegas real-estate appraiser who met Lazar in 1985 and was socialising with him by 1988, and he is the named witness to the three Wednesday-night desert viewings of March and April 1989, the third of which ended with the group detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff. His first-hand claim is about lights seen from Tikaboo Valley and nothing more: he does not claim to have been inside any facility. His second role is that he wrote and co-produced the 1991 videotape, The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible, which is the artefact in which Lazar's whole account is fixed in datable form and which is the strongest opened source in this cluster. That makes him the publisher of the cluster's primary document, and the board treats publication as a structural fact. He is also the source of the $958.11 figure that circulates as the amount on Lazar's W-2: it is his recollection, in his own 1995 synopsis, of a cheque he says he saw.

timeline.label: First Wednesday desert viewing in Tikaboo Valley
timeline.text: Lazar, his wife, Gene Huff and John Lear watched lights in Tikaboo Valley. Mahood's timeline records that only Lear saw an elliptical shape through a telescope. Huff's own synopsis of 12 March 1995 gives the same date.

timeline.label: Third viewing ends with the group detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff
timeline.text: On the third Wednesday viewing the group, which included Lazar, Gene Huff and John Lear, was discovered by guards and detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff. Both the claimants' own accounts and the principal sceptical account agree this happened; they disagree about what the group was watching. Tom Mahood's counter-explanation is that the whole alien-craft narrative began as a cover story after this detention.
